vectors.name: rules
vectors.why: A whole signed document with a rising seq.

vectors.name: rules_by_a_passkey
vectors.why: An owner whose key is a passkey signs rules with WA256.

vectors.name: rules_by_a_passkey_signed_as_a_file_key
vectors.why: Only with WA256.

vectors.name: rules_by_a_passkey_with_another_challenge
vectors.why: The challenge is the hash of these exact rules.

vectors.name: rolled_back
vectors.why: A host can't roll rules back.

vectors.name: one_agent_named_twice
vectors.why: One allowed and one blocked would leave a reader guessing.

vectors.name: one_address_named_twice
vectors.why: Likewise two agents at one address.

vectors.name: contact_naming_an_owner
vectors.why: A contact pins one ID. Who that ID acts for can change, so rules can't name it.

vectors.name: signed_by_the_agent_key
vectors.why: A fooled agent can't change its own rules.

vectors.name: signed_by_another_owner
vectors.why: Only this owner's key counts.

vectors.name: unknown_senders_allowed
vectors.why: There's no allow, so a tricked owner can't remove the floor. Letting people in is the reach setting.

vectors.name: open_to_anyone
vectors.why: An owner can open an agent to anyone, for the types they name.

vectors.name: open_with_no_types
vectors.why: Letting people in with nothing to use means nothing, so it's refused rather than guessed at.

vectors.name: filter_with_nothing_to_match
vectors.why: An empty filter would let nobody in or everybody, depending on the reader.

vectors.name: contacts_only_with_a_filter
vectors.why: A filter only means something when the setting is filter.

vectors.name: filter_host_with_a_path
vectors.why: A host in a filter is a host name, nothing more.

vectors.name: rules_naming_a_delegation
vectors.why: Rules name the one delegation they allow by the hash of its JWS.

vectors.name: rules_naming_a_delegation_another_way
vectors.why: A name has one spelling, so a host and Signet compare it as the owner signed it.

vectors.name: rules_naming_a_delegation_too_long
vectors.why: Nor a longer one.

vectors.name: rules_naming_a_null_delegation
vectors.why: Rules naming none leave the field out, which is its one spelling.

vectors.name: contact_pinned_by_reach
vectors.why: Someone let in by reach isn't a contact, so the owner's rules can't list one as such.

vectors.name: contact_pinned_by_agent
vectors.why: A contact the agent added by itself comes from the two agents' signatures, never from the owner's, so the rules can't list one as such.

vectors.name: agreed_contacts
vectors.why: An owner can let contacts their agent agrees with by itself use the types they name, and text.

vectors.name: agreed_with_no_types
vectors.why: Contacts the agent adds need no type the owner named: the two agents agree what they use.

vectors.name: agreed_naming_cores_own_type
vectors.why: Core's own types aren't the owner's to name: words are text, and agreeing types is agree_types.

vectors.name: contact_named_with_a_type_by_name_alone
vectors.why: A type goes by its fingerprint, so an owner's yes to one is to exactly those rules.

vectors.name: agreed_with_too_many_types
vectors.why: At most 16 types, as for anyone the reach setting lets in.

vectors.name: agreed_with_a_type_twice
vectors.why: Each type once, so no reader guesses what a second one meant.

vectors.name: agreed_with_no_text_setting
vectors.why: Whether words pass is always said.

vectors.name: permission_level_unknown
vectors.why: The levels are ask me, auto within limits and full auto.

vectors.name: quoted_prices_let_go
vectors.why: An owner can let a price their agent quotes, where they'd be paid, go within their limits (Nenye, 2026-11-13, issue 809).

vectors.name: quoted_prices_wait_said
vectors.why: Waiting is the default, which rules usually leave out, and saying it means the same.

vectors.name: quoted_prices_unknown
vectors.why: A quoted price waits or goes within limits, and nothing else is guessed at.

vectors.name: quoted_prices_null
vectors.why: Leaving it out is how to say the default, so null is no spelling of it.

vectors.name: actions_above_the_protocol_cap
vectors.why: An owner can lower the daily actions, never raise them past the protocol's 2,500.

vectors.name: limit_above_the_protocol_cap
vectors.why: Rules can only lower a limit.

vectors.name: limits_on_what_an_agent_sends
vectors.why: An owner can lower what an agent sends through its host.

vectors.name: limit_past_what_most_hosts_allow
vectors.why: Rules can say more than a host allows. It counts the lower of the two, and its operator sets how far that goes.

vectors.name: limit_on_sends_that_isnt_a_count
vectors.why: A count is a whole number, and nothing else can stand in for one.

vectors.name: limits_on_contacts_the_agent_adds
vectors.why: An owner can sign tighter daily limits for contacts their agent adds by itself, and anyone else they haven't named (provisional, 2026-11-14).

vectors.name: limit_on_agreed_texts_above_40
vectors.why: Words with someone the owner hasn't named stay at 40 a day at most, so the setting can only lower it.

vectors.name: limit_on_agreed_new_requests_above_the_cap
vectors.why: New requests from someone the owner hasn't named stay under the same cap as any contact's, so the setting can't lift it.

vectors.name: limit_one_above_the_cap_on_new_requests_per_contact_per_day
vectors.why: Each limit has its own cap, and the first number past it is refused.

vectors.name: limit_one_above_the_cap_on_open_requests_per_contact
vectors.why: Each limit has its own cap, and the first number past it is refused.

vectors.name: limit_one_above_the_cap_on_open_approvals
vectors.why: Each limit has its own cap, and the first number past it is refused.

vectors.name: limit_one_above_the_cap_on_new_from_others_per_day
vectors.why: Each limit has its own cap, and the first number past it is refused.

vectors.name: limit_one_above_the_cap_on_texts_per_contact_per_day
vectors.why: Each limit has its own cap, and the first number past it is refused.

vectors.name: rules_last_until_replaced
vectors.why: Rules with no end last until the owner signs others (Nenye, 2026-11-15).

vectors.name: rules_with_the_old_30_day_end
vectors.why: Rules signed before 2026-11-15 carry the 30 days rules lasted then. It was never the owner's choice, so they still verify past it, and last until replaced.

vectors.name: rules_past_the_end_their_owner_chose
vectors.why: An owner can give rules an end, and past it they stop the agent.

vectors.name: unknown_field
vectors.why: Unknown fields are refused.

vectors.name: signed_for_another_owner
vectors.why: The signature is good, and the document names someone else.

vectors.name: issued_in_the_future
vectors.why: A bad clock on the owner's device can't raise seq out of reach.

vectors.name: end_before_the_start
vectors.why: An end before the issue date is a mistake, not a rule.

vectors.name: rules_applied
vectors.why: Signet says which rules it's running, so a withheld update shows on the owner's page.

vectors.name: rules_applied_by_a_host
vectors.why: A host can't claim Signet applied them.

vectors.name: redeem
vectors.why: The link's private key names who may use the invitation.

vectors.name: host_redeems_for_its_own_agent
vectors.why: A host saw Ben's redeem, and resends it from an agent of its own.

vectors.name: redeem_signed_without_the_link
vectors.why: Whoever lacks the private key can't name a redeemer.

vectors.name: invitation_used_twice
vectors.why: One use.

vectors.name: invitation_expired
vectors.why: Invitations end.

vectors.name: another_invitation
vectors.why: A redeem only fits its own invitation.

vectors.name: another_inviter
vectors.why: A redeem only fits the agent whose link it came from.

vectors.name: allowed_contact
vectors.why: An allowed contact reaches the agent.

vectors.name: unknown_sender
vectors.why: Strangers wait in quarantine. Signet repeats this check, so a host can't push one through.

vectors.name: blocked_sender
vectors.why: A block looks the same as quarantine to the sender.

vectors.name: paused
vectors.why: The kill switch stops everything.

vectors.name: type_this_contact_cant_use
vectors.why: A contact is admitted for its types only.

vectors.name: ended_rules
vectors.why: Past the end their owner chose, rules count as paused.

vectors.name: contact_with_a_new_key
vectors.why: A new key is a new agent ID, so it's a stranger.

vectors.name: open_lets_a_stranger_in
vectors.why: An open agent takes anyone, for the types its owner named.

vectors.name: open_but_another_type
vectors.why: Someone let in gets only the reach setting's types.

vectors.name: open_keeps_a_contacts_own_types
vectors.why: A contact's entry decides its types, whatever the reach setting says.

vectors.name: open_and_blocked
vectors.why: A block beats being open.

vectors.name: open_and_paused
vectors.why: A pause stops everyone, let in or not.

vectors.name: filter_by_owner
vectors.why: The filter names an owner, by what that owner signed for its agent.

vectors.name: filter_by_host
vectors.why: The filter names a host that signed for this delivery, under the key the owner listed for it.

vectors.name: filter_by_a_past_exchange
vectors.why: The filter takes anyone this agent wrote to before.

vectors.name: filter_with_no_match
vectors.why: Anyone else is a stranger, and waits for the owner.

vectors.name: agreed_contact
vectors.why: Someone this agent agreed with by itself, an invite one signed and the other accepted, by the reader's own record of the two signatures, gets the types the owner set for them.

vectors.name: agreed_but_not_turned_on
vectors.why: Rules without the setting give them nothing, so rules signed before it existed don't widen.

vectors.name: agreed_but_another_type
vectors.why: Only the types the owner set for them.

vectors.name: agreed_but_not_by_the_readers_record
vectors.why: Only the reader's record of a pair it checked says so, and nothing a sender sends.

vectors.name: agreed_but_blocked
vectors.why: A block the owner signed beats anything the agent agreed.

vectors.name: agreed_but_removed
vectors.why: So does a removal, which names them with no types.

vectors.name: agreed_but_the_owner_asks_first
vectors.why: At ask me the agent adds no contact by itself, as it sends no invite.

vectors.name: agreed_but_named_with_other_types
vectors.why: A contact the owner named gets the types the owner named, whatever the agent agreed.

vectors.name: agreed_and_paused
vectors.why: A pause stops them too.

vectors.name: contact_opens_a_type_seen_proposed
vectors.why: A contact whose owner lets them agree types opens one this host saw proposed between the two.

vectors.name: contact_opens_a_type_never_proposed
vectors.why: A type nobody proposed between them is no type of theirs, so a key skipping Signet can't name one.

vectors.name: contact_opens_an_agreed_type_with_agreeing_off
vectors.why: The owner's switch decides, whatever was proposed.

vectors.name: contact_opens_a_named_type_with_agreeing_off
vectors.why: A type the owner named for them doesn't need the switch.

vectors.name: contact_proposes_a_type
vectors.why: Agreeing a type needs no owner, where the owner lets them.

vectors.name: contact_proposes_with_agreeing_off
vectors.why: With the switch off they agree nothing new.

vectors.name: contact_proposes_a_named_type_with_agreeing_off
vectors.why: Proposing a type the owner named is how its schema first reaches this agent.

vectors.name: stranger_proposes_a_type_the_owner_named
vectors.why: Someone let in by reach may propose a type the owner named for everyone, and nothing else.

vectors.name: stranger_proposes_another_type
vectors.why: Strangers agree no type of their own.

vectors.name: stranger_opens_a_type_seen_proposed
vectors.why: Seeing one proposed is no switch for someone let in by reach.

vectors.name: invitation_redeemer_opens_its_type
vectors.why: Whoever redeemed an invitation gets the types it names.

vectors.name: invitation_redeemer_proposes_another_type
vectors.why: An invitation is no switch for agreeing types: its redeemer proposes only the types it names.

vectors.name: invitation_redeemer_opens_a_type_seen_proposed
vectors.why: Nor does seeing one proposed let its redeemer open it.

vectors.name: conversation_with_text_off
vectors.why: Core's plain conversation is words someone chose, so it needs the owner's text.

vectors.name: conversation_with_text_on
vectors.why: And goes where the owner turned text on.
